Mysteries.Title:
The First Luminous Mystery

The Baptism of the Lord
Mysteries.SubTitle: Obedience

Meditation.text: A voice cries out in the wilderness.
John the Baptist preaches repentance.
John proclaims that One is coming “the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to unloose.”
Jesus approaches John to be baptized.
John protests that Jesus should be the one baptizing him instead.
Jesus answers that it must be so for now.
The heavens open; the Spirit descends.
A voice from heaven says, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
There is One Lord, One Faith, One Baptism.
We were baptized into His death in order to be raised to new life in Him.

Mysteries.Title:
The Second Luminous Mystery

The Wedding in Cana
Mysteries.SubTitle: Love Others

Meditation.text: There was a marriage in Cana in Galilee.
The wine runs out. Mary intercedes.
Jesus replies that His hour has not yet come.
Mary tells the servants to do whatever He asks.
Jesus asks the jars of water be filled.
The steward marvels that the best wine has been served last.
This was the first of His signs.
“I will espouse thee to Me in faith.”
“Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church”
“Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”

Mysteries.Title:
The Third Luminous Mystery

The Proclamation of the Kingdom of God and the call to conversion
Mysteries.SubTitle: Poverty

Meditation.text: Jesus proclaims, “The Kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the Gospel.”
Jesus preaches the Kingdom in Galilee.
Jesus teaches the Beatitudes to the crowds.
Jesus commands His believers to be salt of the earth and the light of the world.
It is not enough to say “Lord, Lord,” but one must do the will of the Father.
Jesus sends His disciples to preach and say, “The kingdom of heaven is at hand.”
“To other cities also I must preach the kingdom of God: for therefore am I sent.”
If we do not receive the kingdom of God like a little child, neither shall we enter it.
Jesus sends the disciples out to preach the kingdom and heal the sick.
The Apostles preach the Risen Christ.
Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up to a high mountain by themselves.
He is transfigured before them; His face shines like the sun, and His garments shine like light.
Suddenly, Moses and Elijah appear.
Peter asks to build three tents.
As Peter speaks, a cloud descends over them, and the apostles become afraid. Luke 9:34
A voice proclaims of Jesus: “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him.”
The disciples become utterly terrified.
Jesus tells His disciples to rise, and to not be afraid.
As we share in Christ’s sufferings, so shall we share in His glory. 1 Peter 4:13-16
The disciples rejoice to be found worthy to suffer for the sake of His name.

Mysteries.Title:
The Fifth Luminous Mystery

The Institution of the Eucharist
Mysteries.SubTitle: Joy in Finding Jesus

Meditation.text: The Feast of Unleavened Bread, also called the Passover, drew near.
Jesus sends His disciples to make preparations for the Passover.
When evening arrives, Jesus reclines at table with them.
Jesus tells the disciples that He will not share in the Passover again until all is fulfilled.
Our Lord washes the feet of His disciples.
Jesus took the bread, broke it, and gave it to His disciples, saying “This is My Body.”
In a similar way, He took the chalice and said, “This is My Blood.”
“Amen, amen, I say unto you: Except that you eat of the flesh of the Son of Man, and drink His blood, you shall not have life in you.”
For the chalice and bread is a communion in the blood and body of the Lord.
When we eat this bread, and drink this cup, we proclaim His death, until He comes.
